intro.label: Pocket
intro.body: Hats run alone for two bars. Bass enters only on bar 3, and the kick under it is just beats 1 and 3.

intro.label: Figure
intro.body: After the empty opening, three notes arrive: the root on 1, the root again on the and of 2, and down to the minor seventh on the a of 2. None of those attacks has a kick yet.

intro.label: Harmony
intro.body: Am7 (i7) is the only chord in the intro. Its color is A–C–E–G, and the bass does not state it until bar 3.

intro.label: Missable
intro.body: Bars 1 and 2 are hats with no bass. Playing the funk line early covers the silence that makes the entrance.

a1.label: Pocket
a1.body: Groove A keeps the 8th hats but adds a kick on the and of 2 and another on the last 16th. Snare stays on 2 and 4.

a1.label: Figure
a1.body: Offbeat kicks are the new partner. Downbeat root meets one. So does the root on the and of 2. The minor seventh on the a of 2 is the attack left in the crack between those kicks.

a1.label: Harmony
a1.body: Harmony does not move for these eight bars. Am7 keeps the A–C–E–G color while the rhythm section gets busier.

a1.label: Missable
a1.body: The and-of-2 kick is the new event. Leaving it out turns Groove A back into the sparser intro grid.

verse.label: Pocket
verse.body: After D7 the and-of-2 kick and the 8th hats come back with A in the bass. Six bars, not the eight of Groove A.

verse.label: Figure
verse.body: After D7, the first groove's shape is back. Kick shares the downbeat root and the and-of-2 root. Between those, the minor seventh on the a of 2 is unchanged.

verse.label: Harmony
verse.body: D7 lasts through the lift only. Harmony here is Am7 again, so F# from the third no longer belongs.

verse.label: Missable
verse.body: F# belonged to D7. On the return the downbeat is A, and keeping the third from the lift fights Am7.

a2.label: Pocket
a2.body: Same kick grid, denser bass. Ghost snares sit just before the backbeat, and soft bass 16ths answer them. Don't rush a ghost.

a2.label: Figure
a2.body: Register is the story: low root on 1, octave on the a of 1, then the low root returns on the and of 2. Outer notes share kicks. The pop in the middle does not.

a2.label: Harmony
a2.body: The octave pops are still Am7. Nothing in the chord stack changes; only the register and the ghosts are new.

a2.label: Missable
a2.body: The bass ghosts are the quiet 16ths after beat 2, not the downbeat. Playing them as loud as the root on 1 kills the pocket.

b1.label: Pocket
b1.body: The kick pattern stays the Groove A grid, including the and of 2. What moves is the bass root, up to D.

b1.label: Figure
b1.body: A is gone. D is the root on 1 and it locks with the kick. Up to the major third on 2 is F#, the announcement. D returns as the root on the and of 2, and that one locks with the kick too.

b1.label: Harmony
b1.body: This is the first chord change: D7, IV7 in A minor. Bass roots on D and uses F# as the third, not the old A pedal.

b1.label: Missable
b1.body: The D7 bar moves to F# on 2. Easy to play the A from the groove by habit and miss the third.

insight.title: Don't keep the A from Groove A

chorus.label: Pocket
chorus.body: The kick pattern stays the Groove A grid, including the and of 2. What moves is the bass root, up to D.

chorus.label: Figure

a3.body: After D7 the and-of-2 kick and the 8th hats come back with A in the bass. Six bars, not the eight of Groove A.

a3.label: Figure
a3.body: After D7, the first groove's shape is back. Kick shares the downbeat root and the and-of-2 root. Between those, the minor seventh on the a of 2 is unchanged.

a3.label: Harmony
a3.body: D7 lasts through the lift only. Harmony here is Am7 again, so F# from the third no longer belongs.

a3.label: Missable
a3.body: F# belonged to D7. On the return the downbeat is A, and keeping the third from the lift fights Am7.

br.label: Pocket
br.body: Hats drop from every 8th to quarters, and the kick leaves the offbeats. Snare clusters at the end of the bar instead of a plain 2 and 4.

br.label: Figure
br.body: E7 is the chord and the bass will not play E. Fourth on 1 sits in a kick. Fourth on 3 sits in the other kick. The octave on 4 is the only higher A, and it is kickless.

br.label: Harmony
br.body: Three bars of E7, the V7. The bass pedals A, the fourth, so the dominant is in the chord while the bass refuses the root.

br.label: Missable
br.body: E7 wants an E in your ear. The written bass stays on A, the fourth, on 1 and on 3. An early E jumps the return.

bridge.label: Pocket
bridge.body: Hats drop from every 8th to quarters, and the kick leaves the offbeats. Snare clusters at the end of the bar instead of a plain 2 and 4.

bridge.label: Figure
bridge.body: E7 is the chord and the bass will not play E. Fourth on 1 sits in a kick. Fourth on 3 sits in the other kick. The octave on 4 is the only higher A, and it is kickless.

bridge.label: Missable

out.label: Pocket
out.body: The offbeat kick grid returns, but the bass shrinks to three long notes a bar. Let the kit carry the 16ths.

out.label: Figure
out.body: Only A, and plenty of space around it. The root on 1 is a long one, the root again on 3 answers it, and the octave on the and of 4 is a short tag. The first two share the kick; the tag does not.

out.label: Harmony
out.body: E7 is over. The outro sits on Am7 with long A roots and no further chord move.

out.label: Missable
out.body: Groove A's subdivisions do not belong in the outro. Three A attacks are the whole bar; a fill between them crowds the ending.
